reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself. I'll start by listing the orders.
Next I'll check the refunds list to confirm the refund amounts before computing any payouts.

The refund list matches the handoff: orders 150, 151, and 155 each have the reported amounts. The customers in this batch are acme, birch, and cobalt, so I'll get each one's net balance before paying.
acme's net of 9958 matches my own check: orders 150 and 153 total 22640, minus the 12682 refund on order 150. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
birch's net of 42141 matches my check: orders 151 and 154 total 58011, minus the 15870 refund on order 151. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

I've checked all three customers. Cobalt's net of 50848 matches my check: orders 152 and 155 total 55057, minus the 4209 refund on order 155. Every net balance agrees with my own arithmetic, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
acme's payout of 9958 was recorded and matches my own check. birch's net of 42141 also matches: orders 151 and 154 total 58011, minus the 15870 refund on order 151. I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net of 50848 matches my own check: orders 152 and 155 total 55057, minus the 4209 refund on order 155. acme and birch are already paid, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three customers have been paid. Each net balance matched my own check against the orders and refunds, and every record_payout returned ok.
